create.name: Dr. Raj Balkaran
create.bio:
Raj Balkaran is a scholar of Sanskrit storytelling who brings the myths and wisdom teachings of ancient India to yoga students and general audiences. After a master's degree in Toronto and Sanskrit study in Pune, he completed a doctorate in religion at the University of Calgary in 2015. He has since taught Hinduism and Indian mythology at several Canadian universities and, from 2020, on the continuing education courses of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. His academic books for Routledge look at the Goddess and the sun in the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, while The Stories Behind the Poses (2022) retells the legends behind fifty yoga postures and is now used in many teacher trainings.

He sees himself as a teacher within a living lineage as much as an academic. In 2021 he started The Indian Wisdom School, an online school whose courses cover the Goddess traditions, the stories of Śiva and Viṣṇu, the Bhagavad Gītā, mantra and yoga philosophy, alongside a free weekly Gītā study circle. He has recorded hundreds of interviews with scholars of South Asia for a New Books Network podcast on Indian religions, guides pilgrimages to temples in India and residential retreats in other countries, and offers one-to-one life guidance online rooted in the Indian texts. He spent four years as chaplain of Indian spirituality at McMaster University.

books.title: The Stories Behind the Poses: The Indian Mythology That Inspired 50 Yoga Postures
books.author: Raj Balkaran
books.description: An illustrated guide pairing fifty yoga postures with the Indian myths behind their names, from the warrior to the monkey god Hanumān, and drawing out what each story offers a practitioner. Published by Leaping Hare Press in 2022 and used in many yoga teacher trainings.

books.title: The Goddess and the Sun in Indian Myth
books.author: Raj Balkaran
books.description: A scholarly study in the Routledge Hindu Studies series that reads the praise texts of the Goddess and of the sun god in the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa side by side. It argues that the two were designed to mirror one another around themes of power and preservation.

courses.title: The Stories Behind the Poses: Mythology in Motion
courses.description: A weekend at Esalen in Big Sur that turns the myths behind yoga postures into lived experience. Tales of the sages and of gods such as Śiva, Indra and Hanumān are explored through breath, posture and presence, following an arc from the qualities that support practice to surrender. No prior study of mythology or Sanskrit is needed.

courses.title: The Elemental Ascent: The Journey from Earth to Ether
courses.description: A four-module online course on the five great elements of Indian thought, earth, water, fire, air and ether, and how they shape the cosmos, body and mind in the Indian wisdom traditions. It carries ten hours of Yoga Alliance continuing education credit.

courses.title: Sounding the Sacred: The Goddess Hymns of the Devī Māhātmya
courses.description: Four modules, each given to one of the great Goddess hymns of the Devī Māhātmya, read line by line for meaning and purpose. Aimed at anyone who chants these hymns or would like to.

courses.title: Sacred Storytelling Workshop: How Myth Teaches Without Teaching
courses.description: A recorded two-hour workshop on how Indian myths guide listeners through structure and symbol rather than instruction, using the stories of Satī, Sāvitrī and Naciketas.

courses.title: All Access Membership
courses.description: Membership of The Indian Wisdom School giving access to its full library of past and future courses on yoga philosophy, Sanskrit narratives, mantra and the Goddess traditions.
courses.price: $47 USD per month or $497 USD per year

courses.title: Life Guidance Sessions
courses.description: Weekly or occasional one-hour online sessions that apply the Gītā, the Upaniṣads and the epics to practical questions of work, relationships and vocation. Session packs are offered at lower rates, and a free discovery call comes first.

free_resources.title: Wisdom Wednesdays
free_resources.description: A free weekly live study of the Bhagavad Gītā, taken verse by verse with teaching and open discussion. Members can also watch more than two hundred hours of earlier sessions.

free_resources.title: Goddess Stories
free_resources.description: A four-part video course on the myths behind eight goddess-inspired yoga poses, based on his book, with downloadable notes. Currently offered free after sign-up.

flags: Name kept as 'Dr. Raj Balkaran', as he presents himself on his site and school (he is widely called 'Dr. Raj'); his doctorate is in religion.

Instagram and YouTube accounts are branded The Indian Wisdom School / The Indian Wisdom Podcast; they are his own one-teacher school, so they were counted and linked. Facebook and X counts could not be read.
No email is published (the only address on his site is a 'user@domain.com' form placeholder); the contact form on rajbalkaran.com is used.
Both photos look heavily retouched or AI-enhanced studio portraits; they match each other and the Esalen page, but a human may want to check.
Goddess Stories is marked 'free for a limited time'; it may become paid.
Life Guidance sessions use coaching framing (he holds ICF certification); kept because the work is rooted in Indian wisdom texts and makes no health claims.
left_out: The Goddess and the King in Indian Myth (Routledge 2019): amazon.com /dp/ page returned 500, so the listing could not be verified.
The Severed Head course (modules from 20 Nov 2026): price not published on the page.
Sacred Sites of Shiva pilgrimage (Sept 2026), Banff and Los Angeles retreats (2026): already past.
Intermediate Sanskrit Reading Group (Devī Māhātmya translation, $67 USD per month): needs prior Sanskrit; list kept to six offerings.
Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies courses and university teaching: run by those institutions.
Indian Myths and Legends (Flame Tree): he wrote the introduction only; Visions and Revisions in Sanskrit Narrative: co-edited, open access, no Amazon check.
New Books in Indian Religions podcast: interviews of other scholars, not his teaching.
